summary: This paper presents a complete bidirectional cryogenic analog signal processing architecture operating at 4 K for superconducting qubit control and readout, featuring a PLL-based I/Q modulator, power amplifier, LNA with 14 dB gain, and 8-PSK demodulator. All circuits are validated through LTSpice simulations with 180 nm cryogenic MOSFET models, achieving I/Q phase error below 2°, image rejection exceeding 35 dB, and symbol error rate below $10^{-6}$.
motivation: Conventional room-temperature control electronics routed via coaxial cables to millikelvin quantum processors introduce prohibitive thermal load ($\sim 10$ µW per line), latency, and wiring complexity that limit scaling beyond 100 qubits. Integrating signal processing at 4 K reduces the thermal footprint to the mixing chamber while enabling tighter feedback for quantum error correction.
method: A complete bidirectional signal chain was designed using standard CMOS topology: control path implements XOR-based PLL, VCO with 50 kΩ and 10 pF RC elements, I/Q modulator with third-order RC lowpass filter ($40$ dB harmonic rejection) and all-pass quadrature shifter achieving 90° phase accuracy, and binary-weighted DAC; readout path features LT1028 LNA (0.9 nV/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ input noise) with gain set to 5 V/V and flash ADC. All simulations employed cryogenic MOSFET models capturing carrier freeze-out, threshold voltage elevation, and 75× thermal noise reduction at 4 K.
result: PLL achieves phase lock within 2 ms with residual error $<0.5°$ RMS; I/Q amplitude imbalance $<0.3$ dB yields image rejection ratio $>35$ dB; 8-PSK demodulation achieves symbol error rate $<10^{-6}$; steady-state power consumption of 199.7 mW scales to approximately 88 mW projected at 65 nm node, offering $5\times$ efficiency over Delta-Sigma approaches and reducing thermal budget utilization from 20% to 9%.
